- Solution-processed semiconductors
- Hybrid nanostructures and functional materials
- Perovskite and emerging solar cells
- Charge transport and recombination
- Optical and electronic characterization
- Structure–property relationships

Name: Artificial Living Brain Lab
Description:
The Artificial Living Brain Laboratory is a research lab pioneering the development of next-generation Neural Processing Units (NPUs) for autonomous robotic systems. Our mission is to create radically energy-efficient NPUs, optimized for mobile platforms.

Our NPUs are based on non-biological, artificial living materials that replicate the functionality of biological neural networks—enabling unprecedented energy efficiency, adaptability, and cognitive capacity.

This breakthrough technology has the potential to disrupt the AI hardware market, expand the frontier of mobile drones, and create an entirely new category of intelligent robots capable of operating autonomously in complex environments.

Market Opportunity

The global market for NPUs is expanding rapidly, with companies like NVIDIA reaching historic valuations. However, conventional silicon-based architectures face serious constraints in power consumption, adaptability, and scalability—especially for mobile and embedded systems. To unlock the next stage of AI evolution, new materials and architectures are required.

Our lab addresses this gap by developing NPUs that are:

•	Radically energy-efficient, enabling continuous real-time processing on mobile platforms
•	Cognitively advanced, thanks to a neural architecture inspired by living systems
•	Scalable and manufacturable, using processes compatible with existing semiconductor fabrication

Investment Thesis
We are seeking strategic investment to:
1.	Scale fabrication capabilities for prototype NPUs
2.	Expand our core team with specialists in AI hardware and neural systems
3.	Accelerate technology validation through integration into robotic platforms
4.	Protect and commercialize IP through patents and licensing

These products are being used to provide the necessary amounts of trace elements to the plants, which, thanks to their physical and chemical properties, are more bioavailable.

The key is the higher surface area of the materials within our fertilizers that provides more reaction site among the molecules, which facilitates the metabolic reactions in the plant system.

The reduced size of the particles allows more opportunity of contact per unit area, which leads to more penetration into the plant and uptake of nutrients.

This technology allows the use of very small amounts of fertilizer material to cover a large area, which helps saving resources and have less environmental impact. Our concept provides perfect tools for sustainable agriculture.

Name: NanoFocus, Inc.
Description:
NanoFocus, Inc. provides 3-D surface metrology and micro-geometry measurement solutions that are cost-effective, robust and user-friendly. Applications include surface finish, surface topography and micro-geometry quantification for quality control, process control and R&D. Market segments include Solar, Renewables, Automotive, Electronics, Medical, Manufacturing & Tools, Micro-systems, Printing and Paper.

NanoFocus offers four product lines to its customers all of which can be customized to offer a tailor-fit measurement solution:

μsurf Technology – NanoFocus pioneered the application of spinning disc confocal technology to surface metrology and continues to lead with market segment with technology refinements that none of our competitors can offer. Based on spinning disc confocal technology, μsurf technology provides the fastest high resolution surface height data of almost any surface, allowing the μsurf system to measure nearly any surface even if it is very rough, highly polished, transparent, or light absorbing (up to 99%). 

μscan Technology – Scanning surface metrology solutions are “a dime a dozen” in the current market, thus NanoFocus offers more than just sensors and a controller, we offer integrated measurement solutions. From fully automated robotic systems to feed back systems that control production line operation variables, μscan technology based systems are built to customer specifications for customer needs.

μsprint – High speed confocal surface metrology just got faster. New high speed sensors that can be operated in mulit-channel mode leaves other metrology sensors in the starting blocks. μsprint technology is offered as a standalone measurement platform or as an OEM sensor package that is integrated into existing manufacturing or inspection installations.

μsoft – Powerful software built on a platform flexible enough to handle any measurement and analysis is the hallmark of μsoft technology.

Name: epiray GmbH

Thermal Laser Epitaxy (TLE) is a new deposition technology that will significantly impact thin film research and production.
TLE adds significant flexibility and speed to thin-film research. Targets can be changed on a daily basis, and almost any material can be used. Layers of ultra-high purity can be deposited. Multiple cheap chambers can be used in parallel with one set of lasers, thus widely different materials can be used in parallel. Operating cost are low. It allows to conduct many more experiments in a given timeframe, with more diverse elements, than any other epitaxy method on the market.

Drug discovery demands reliable, ultrasensitive and fast techniques to test small drug volumes. The efficacy and biotoxicity of drugs is heavily affected by their chiral configuration. In turn, pharmaceutical companies routinely encounter a looking-glass world of mirror-image molecules – enantiomers - where chiral sensing of small drug volumes plays a pivotal role for drug discovery and nanomedicine. 

TwistedNano addresses this need with a new generation of integrated nanophotonic devices enabling the characterization of small quantities of chiral drugs with volumes of a few nanolitres through light, revolutionizing at source the technological toolbox for drug discovery and nanomedicine.

Name: Deutsche Plattform NanoBioMedizin (DP-NBM)
Description:
Trotz immenser Fortschritte in der modernen Medizin besteht immer noch großer Bedarf an neuen diagnostischen und therapeutischen Innovationen, um Krankheiten früher und gezielter diagnostizieren sowie besser und kostengünstiger therapieren zu können.

Eine Schlüsseltechnologie auf diesem Weg ist die Nanotechnologie, weil sie einerseits die Instrumente für eine noch detailliertere Analyse und ein daraus resultierendes besseres Verständnis der Krankheitsursachen und -abläufe liefert, und andererseits die Materialien zur Verfügung stellt, Krankheiten gezielter behandeln zu können. 

Megatrends wie Personalisierte oder Regenerative Medizin sind ohne nanotechnologische Lösungen nicht zu realisieren. 

Die Integration der Nanotechnologie in biomedizinische Anwendungen, kurz NanoBioMedizin genannt, erfordert neue Forschungsdisziplin übergreifende Konzepte und Wertschöpfungsketten. Dazu müssen Technologieentwickler aus den Materialwissenschaften, Chemie, Biologie und Physik mit medizinischen Anwendern wie Pharmazeuten, Klinikern und Industrieunternehmen zusammenarbeiten, um am Ende bedarfsgerechte Innovationen für Patienten auf den Markt bringen zu können. Als Rahmen für den erforderlichen Dialog all dieser Akteure ist eine deutsche NanoBioMedizin Plattform gegründet worden. Das Ziel, das mit dieser Plattform erreicht werden soll, ist eine integrierte Forschungsförderung von der Nanomaterialentwicklung bis zur Klinik, mit der das zweifellos vorhandene wissenschaftliche und wirtschaftliche Potenzial in der deutschen NanoBioMedizin durch nachhaltige Forschungsthemen und Strukturen weiterentwickelt werden kann. Es soll eine Spitzenposition Deutschlands in dieser Zukunftstechnologie erreicht und gefestigt werden.

Name: TECHNO-CLS Project
Description: TECHNO-CLS project aims at the breakthrough in technologies needed for designing and practical realisation of novel gamma-ray Light Sources (LS) operating at photon energies from keV up to GeV range that can be constructed through exposure of oriented crystals (linear, bent and periodically bent) to the beams of ultra-relativistic charged particles. The TECHNO-CLS high-risk/high-gain science-towards-technology breakthrough research programme will address the physics of the processes accompanying the oriented crystal exposure to irradiation by the high-energy electron and positron beams at the atomistic level of detail needed for the realisation of the TECHNO-CLS goals. A broad interdisciplinary, international collaboration has been created previously in the frame of FP7 and H2020 projects, which performed initial experimental tests to demonstrate the crystalline undulator (CU) idea, production and characterisation of periodically bent crystals and the related theory. Additionally, by means of a pre-bunched beam a CU LS has a potential to generate coherent superradiant radiation with wavelengths orders of magnitudes less than 1 Angstrom, i.e. within the range that cannot be reached in existing LSs based on magnetic undulators. Such LSs will have many applications in the basic sciences including nuclear and solid-state physics and the life sciences. Theoretical, computational, experimental and technological results obtained in the course of this project will pave a way for key technological developments of the LSs and their wide exploitation. The TECHNO-CLS international collaboration possesses all the necessary expertise to successfully conduct the outlined programme.

The product line of mechOnics AG ranges from these stand-alone simple positioning components for laboratory applications to complete automated and integrated solutions for low temperature-positioning. The product range includes different sizes and travel of the stages for ambient temperature up to low temperature operation.
 
The product range is completed by innovative and highly flexible control systems for multiple axes operation.

As a market leader for micro-/nanopositioning devices we continuously work on supporting our customers to achieve reliable scientific results efficiently. Thus, our aim is to open up new possibilities ranging from scientific research to industrial applications.
 
Linear positioners are available with travel ranges up to 50 mm for ambient temperatures and UHV applications, for cryogenic application linear stages up to 20 mm can be delivered. Description: "Der Splitter im Auge meines Gegenüber ist leicht zu erkennen, das eigene Brett vorm Kopf dagegen sehr schwer." Das Zitat von Rolf Neijman nehme ich immer wieder gern als gedankliche Vorlage, um zunächst natürlich meine situative Kommunikation zu prüfen und direkt zu reflektieren als auch in meinen Beratungen, weitestgehend die Betrachter Rolle einnehmen zu können. Name: ACEworks
Description:

We are able to deliver complete atomistic simulation workflows for specific materials and applications, from the generation of comprehensive reference data to detailed analysis of simulation outcomes.

Name: Hybrid Quantum Systems
Description: We are the Quantum Optics group of Prof. Dr. Alexander Kubanek at Ulm University, exploring solid-state quantum emitters for future quantum networks. A key goal is to build efficient light–matter interfaces by integrating these emitters in nanophotonic and open Fabry-Perot cavities, enabling controlled emission into well-defined optical modes.

Name: Physics of Low Dimensional Systems

Name: AMSwitch
Description:
AMSwitch is developing a new class of ultra‐low‐power logic switches using altermagnetic materials—an emerging magnetic state with zero net magnetization but electrically readable signals. These devices could operate below 1 aJ per bit, approaching fundamental energy limits.


The project explores two concepts: a gate‐tunable altermagnet switch using Berry‐curvature control, and a current‐driven switch that flips the altermagnetic order for compact logic operations. Together, they aim to enable reliable, non‐volatile, and energy‐efficient computing for future edge devices.


AMSwitch unites experts across materials science, nanoscale fabrication, device engineering, quantum theory, synchrotron characterization, and magnetometry—ensuring rapid progress from discovery to technology.


AMSwitch is coordinated by Chalmers University of Technology and has received funding from the European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA) under the European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under Grant Agreement n° 101258102.

Nanosurf -- Zoom into the Future

Our bespoke solutions not only meet the unique needs of each client but also enhance efficiency and precision in their production lines.

Established in 1997, Nanosurf defined ease of use in scanning probe microscopy by miniaturizing the size of a scanning probe microscope to fit a coffee table. Since then, the Swiss-based company has matured into one of the leading innovators in atomic force microscopy. Nanosurf provides continually evolving instrument platforms for academic researchers and industry applications in life science and materials science, as well as large-scale customized industrial solutions for use in production lines with very demanding accuracy specifications.

Nanosurf will continue to focus development efforts on new measurement modes and technologies that make atomic force microscopes an easier, faster, and more reliable tool. It is also our mission to bring the technique to an ever-increasing range of new application areas by making it as accessible and intuitive to new users as more common technologies such as optical microscopy. Together, we tackle the challenge.

Nanosurf is part of Lab14 Group, a group of successful high-tech companies providing advanced manufacturing solutions with complementary products and services for a wide range of applications that require demanding solutions for nano- and microfabrication and surface analysis.

nanoXIM•Oral Care: The key hydroxyapatite ingredients for oral care applications, to reduce dental hypersensitivity, enhance enamel remineralization and restore natural whiteness. 
Available in two different forms: water suspension (nano) and powder (micro).

nanoXIM•Medical: Synthetic highly pure hydroxyapatite (HAp) and tricalcium phosphate (TCP) materials for bone regeneration medical devices. 
Available in three different forms: pastes, powders and granules.

nanoXIM•Food: The key hydroxyapatite ingredients for functional food and food supplements, to promote bone strength, reduce bone loss and prevent dental hypersensitivy. 
Available in two different forms: water suspension (nano) and powder (micro).

nanoXIM•Research: Looking for a calcium phosphate for your research? nanoXIM products are also available for several research fields including bio-separation, catalysis, pharma, biotechnology and functionalized textiles.

Name: XRnanotech
Description: XRnanotech is an award-winning Swiss deep tech company. We offer innovative nanostructured X-ray optics with outstanding precision for high-tech applications. Our optics allow to focus ever higher-energy beams onto the smallest possible samples. This is crucial for drug discovery, medical imaging, microchip inspection or investigation of advanced materials. In this niche, we provide unique solutions for several hundred large-scale R&D beamlines and high-tech companies around the world. Our vision is to enable them to analyze yet unmeasurable nano-systems.

Name: SmarAct Group
Description:
With the development and production of market-leading solutions in the field of high-precision positioning, automation and metrology, the SmarAct Group reliably accompanies its customers. The broad product portfolio ranges from single positioners to complex parallel kinematics, miniaturized robots, controllers and measurement technology and is complemented by automated microassembly solutions.  

Since its founding in 2005, SmarAct has grown from a small team of engineers to a group of companies with three independent business units and over 250 highly skilled members. Today, SmarAct relies on years of experience and, above all, on a very passionate team with unconditional customer focus.

Name: SOL instruments GmbH
Description:
SOL instruments GmbH. is an innovation-focused manufacturer of technologically advanced instruments for light measuring, elemental analysis and nano-scale microscopy.

For two decades we have devoted our knowledge, innovations and experience to spectroscopy, microscopy, lasers and create robust tools for scientific and industrial applications in three business segments:

 -  Analysis
 -  Spectroscopy
 -  Lasers

We are proud to be a part of the world's most advanced scientific explorations and bring our innovations to the market of high performance equipment.

We are striving to be a reliable supplier of high-tech products and innovative solutions for customers' advanced needs and to offer top-level technical service and support all over the world.

Name: Hitachi High-Tech Europe
Description:
Hitachi High-Tech Europe is a market-leading provider of high-tech solutions for industry and academia, covering materials science, life sciences, biotechnology, industrial automation, and nanotechnology.

Our diverse product lineup includes electron microscopes (SEM/TEM/FIB), nano-technology solutions for semiconductor manufacturing, clinical analyzers, biotechnology products and radiation therapy systems. We also provide high value-added solutions to industries fields such as mobility, connectivity, environment and energy. 

Through our core Observation, Measurement, and Analysis technologies, we’re committed to contributing to the realisation of a sustainable society by solving social issues.

Name: Quantum Design Microscopy
Description:
For more than 40 years Quantum Design (QD) has been providing technology solutions to researchers in the fields of physics, chemistry, biotechnology, materials science, and nanotechnology. Established in 1982 in San Diego, California, Quantum Design is the leading commercial source for automated materials characterization systems offering a variety of measurement capabilities. 

QD instruments are found in the world’s leading research institutions and have become the reference standard for a variety of magnetic and physical property measurements. Quantum Design instruments are cited in, and provide the data for, more scientific publications than any other instrument in the fields of magnetics and materials characterization. This means that each year, literally hundreds of scientific publications, advancing the science of materials, use data generated from QD instruments. 

An essential part of providing scientific solutions to researchers around the globe is to also offer state-of-the-art instruments from other leading manufacturers. These manufacturers are chosen by Quantum Design not only for their innovative products, but also because they believe in the same level of customer satisfaction and support that scientists have come to expect from QD products worldwide. 

With headquarters in the USA, and offices in Belgium, Brazil, China, Czech Republic, Germany, France, Hungary, India, Italy, Japan, Korea, Poland, Romania, Russia, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Turkey, and the United Kingdom, QD is strategically located in the world’s key centers for scientific research, providing local marketing, sales, and technical support.

Name: Obducat Group
Description: Obducat is an innovative developer and world-leading supplier of micro-and nano lithography solutions. We supply technology, products and processes used for advanced micro- and nanopatterning of surfaces. By changing surface properties through patterning, new areas of application are made possible as well as increased device performance. Obducat’s technologies include nano imprint technology, coating technology and wet processing technology. Our technologies are successfully used by companies within the LED, OLED, semiconductor, display, optical and photonics, biomedical and MEMS industries. Obducat has offices in Sweden, Germany and China and the headquarter is located in Lund, Sweden. Obducat’s shares are publicly traded on the Swedish NGM Main Regulated Equity stock exchange.

Name: cfaed - Center for Advancing Electronics Dresden
Description:
Research Cluster at TU Dresden within DRESDEN_concept. Joined forces to explore new technologies for information processing.
Impressum: http://bit.ly/23ejDr7

Inspired by the huge impact of semiconductor technology, the researchers of our cluster have thus joined forces to explore new technologies for electronic information processing which overcome the limits of today's predominant CMOS technology. As this topic is on the agenda of all relevant scientific and industrial organizations, we focus on well-chosen approaches which reflect the research excellence of Dresden.

Cluster Speaker: Prof. Thomas Mikolajick

Name: Particle Metrix GmbH
Description:
Particle Metrix is a leading provider of advanced particle analysis solutions specializing in high-precision nanoparticle tracking technology. Based in Inning am Ammersee near Munich, we bridge the gap between complex nanoscale challenges and actionable data.

Our expert team develops instruments that set industry standards for accuracy and efficiency, empowering researchers in pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, environmental science, and materials research to push the boundaries of what is possible. Whether you are investigating extracellular vesicles, viruses, LNPs, nanobubbles, or novel nanomaterials, we provide the clarity and reproducibility you need. With a strong focus on innovation and quality, Particle Metrix delivers reliable tools that support scientific progress.

Why partner with us?
 Innovative Precision: Technology that turns complex particle samples into clear, reliable insights.
 Scientific Partnership: We are more than a supplier; we are your dedicated support team for every step of your analytical journey.
 Quality Made in Germany: Precision engineering for the most demanding research applications.

Join our community and stay updated on the latest trends in nanoparticle analysis.

Name: neaspec
Description:
neaspec designs, manufactures and distributes advanced nanoscale optical imaging & spectroscopy microscopes.

The company was founded to revolutionize nanoscale analytics, with the ultimate goal to enable technological & scientific progress in every lab around the world.

neaspec has gained worldwide attention in the scientific community for inventing a series of breakthrough technologies in nanoscale analytics. Founded in 2007 by the world’s leading experts of near-field microscopy as a spin-off from the the Max-Planck-Institute of Biochemistry, neaspec’s engineers have developed the neaSNOM microscope, an easy-to-use optical near-field microscope platform using ground-breaking and patented optical background-filtering techniques.

neaSNOM closes a nanoanalytical gap by combining the best of two worlds – the nanoscale resolution of atomic force microscopy (AFM) with the analytical power of visible, infrared and even THz imaging & spectroscopy. At a spatial resolution of only 10nm, the method only requires standard AFM sample preparation and is non-destructive. This opens a new era for modern nano-analytical applications such as chemical nano-identification (IR), nano-plasmonic field mapping (VIS & IR) or free charge carrier nano-mapping (THz).

Name: Bruker BioAFM
Description:
Bruker's BioAFM expertise has its roots in the extensive development capabilities of JPK Instruments AG, which joined the Bruker Nano Surfaces and Metrology division in 2018. JPK was founded in 1999 as a spin-off from Humboldt University in Berlin, Germany,  and quickly established itself as a pioneer in the commercial development of atomic force microscopy (AFM) and optical tweezers for life science applications.

Key JPK innovations that set new industry benchmarks include:

The ability to investigate challenging biological samples (e.g., living cells and tissues) in liquid and under controlled environmental conditions;
High-speed scanning capabilities that enable the real-time visualization of dynamic molecular mechanisms;
Multiparametric quantification of nanomechanical properties, such as adhesion and stiffness; and
The ability to combine BioAFM instruments with advanced optical microscopy techniques, such as confocal and super-resolution microscopy.
JPK's flagship product line, NanoWizard BioAFMs, launched in 2001 and has remained at the forefront of innovation in biomolecular and cellular imaging. The ForceRobot and  CellHesion systems launched in 2007 and 2008, respectively, and specialized on single molecule force and single cell spectroscopy. Finally, the NanoTracker optical tweezers system launched in 2013.

Since 2018, these technologies have been integrated with Bruker's proprietary advances, such as PeakForce Tapping, and worldwide reach to deliver the highest performance commercial BioAFMs avilable today.

Currently, more than 30 working groups from physics, chemistry and engineering are involved. To achieve our goals, we operate a shared research building in Hanover.

Name: German BioImaging - Gesellschaft für Mikroskopie und Bildanalyse e.V.
Description:
Microscopy and the quantitative analysis of microscopic images lie at the heart of modern biomedical sciences and are a motor of technological innovations. 

German BioImaging - Gesellschaft für Mikroskopie und Bildanalyse e.V. (GerBI-GMB, Society for Microscopy and Image Analysis) is a scientific society representing the interests of researchers and professionals as well as core facilities in Germany involved in microscopy and image data analysis for the life sciences. 

The society fosters knowledge exchange within the community, and interaction between scientists and engineers both from academia and industry. Additionally, GerBI-GMB promotes communication with the public about imaging in the life sciences.

Name: n.able GmbH i.L.
Description:
n.able is a spin-off company born at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology in the Institute of Nanotechnology. 
Having more than 10 years experience in functionalization of surfaces at the nano- and microscales, we have developed an innovative Molecular Printer. It's dedicated for fast surface and device functionalization with variety of inks. The flexibility to use various inks on our printer will allow you to create microarrays in a fast way, covering large areas (dm2) with a possibility to quality check the samples with in built microscope.
Along with the Molecular Desktop Printer, we offer various consumables and a variety of services related to surface functionalization.

High Power Actuators for pulse generation, fatigue testing, shaker systems, and vibration testing.

The company was founded by Prof. Alfred Benninghoven, Dr. Ewald Niehuis and Mr. Thomas Heller in 1989 to commercialise the original research carried out by Prof. Benninghoven and his team at the University of Muenster in Germany from the early 80's. Since the technique became commercially viable IONTOF has made many product improvements and more than 400 instruments are in operation in industrial and academic laboratories worldwide.
Today, the IONTOF group consists of four different companies. The IONTOF GmbH, which sells, produces and services all IONTOF analytical instruments. The IONTOF Technologies GmbH which is in charge of all R&D projects. The subsidiaries IONTOF USA and IONTOF Japan which were founded for sales and after sales service in the United States (founded 2000) and Japan (founded 2022).

ORELTECH is an innovation leader and expert in metallization and functional surface coating.

Today, the core of ORELTECH’s success is the proprietary formula of nanoparticle-free metal solutions, which has grown into an extensive library of unique formulations developed for specific technological challenges, and a committed tech team with combined 25+ years of experience in chemical research and product development. 

Customer and market needs have led ORELTECH to develop solutions to metallization challenges in industries including printed electronics, PCB production, photovoltaics, medical coatings, catalytic and antibacterial layers, plating on plastics and smart textiles.

Together with our customers, we get to the core of any metallization challenge, tailor our products and optimize the production process to meet their specific demands. We are satisfied when the customer masters our technology in mass production.

Magnetron Technology – sputtering specialist for highend PVD coatings

Our specialists offer a broad coating knowhow in various fields of science and technology in the areas of optics and semiconductor industry, space technology and neutron physics.

Our techniques include DC-, RF- and reactive magnetron sputtering of a large variety of materials on different substrates including glass, metal (-foils) and silicon wafers surfaces.

We are experts in magnetic field simulations and design, construct and manufacture customized magnetron sputter sources for complex geometries.

Coating analysis technologies like XRD, XRR, GID and transmission/reflectivity measurements are used in our lab.

Name: ZMN @ TU Ilmenau
Description:
The ZMN is the Center of Micro- and Nanotechnologies at the TU Ilmenau. Since 2006 it exists as a central operating unit of the university and as a technological center for the associated Institute of Micro- and Nanotechnologies (IMN MacroNano).
The foundation of the interfaculty research center was already driven by 9 departments in the mid 90s of the last century. With the aim of providing the community of researchers and university staff with a place for top-level interdisciplinary research, the high-tech building Feynmanbau was opened as ZMN in 2002. With the acquisition of a second building by the TU Ilmenau, the Meitnerbau, further (clean room) areas could be developed for the center.

The main task of the ZMN is to support and promote scientists in the field of micro- and nanotechnology. The ZMN fulfills this task by purchasing equipment and new facilities, operating and maintaining them, and through financial project management. In particular, the support and technological safeguarding of the equipment is organized in close coordination with the technologically driving departments of the center and institute.

As a "Core Facility", the ZMN provides direct access to its infrastructure as well as the possibility to provide processes as services. The Center is open to the research community of the TU Ilmenau as well as to external researchers from academia and industry.

The physical proximity of the various departments and research groups creates an intensive scientific exchange in a creative environment. Interdisciplinarity is lived at the ZMN.

Schaefer Scientific (formerly Schaefer Technologie) is a trusted partner in scientific and engineering innovation since 1963. With a presence in five European countries, we specialize in marketing and supporting cutting-edge technologies across a wide range of scientific fields.

As one of Europe’s leading trading and consulting companies, we represent top-tier manufacturers in Germany and across the continent. Name: FOCUS · SPECSGROUP
Description:
Focus is a brand of SPECSGROUP and the Lab14 group of companies, with its facility located in Hünstetten, close to Frankfurt, Germany. It stands for technological top-tier components for Electron Spectroscopy in Surface Science, one of the world's most complex research areas. 

Since it was established in 1990 under the identical company name, Focus is driven by a highly educated and motivated team of physicists and engineers committed to pushing the boundaries of solutions for new materials research. A major product launch was made in 1998 with the introduction of the first commercial Time-of-Flight Photoemission Electron Microscope (TOF-PEEM), followed by the patented NanoESCA in 2005, a system that significantly enhanced energy resolution for imaging. 

In 2006, Focus pioneered the integration of Momentum Microscopy using NanoESCA & TOF-PEEM. It marked a milestone in the visualization of electronic band structures. Furthermore in 2011 the first commercial VLEED detector for highly sensitive spin-polarization measurements was released. 

Focus`strong commitment to technological leadership continues with the newest generation of instruments, such as the advanced TOF-MARIS introduced in 2023, which refines Time-of-Flight momentum microscopy.

The dedication of Focus to drive innovation is reflected by a deep connection to the global research community.

Name: ANTACON GmbH
Description:
Wir bieten neuartige, hoch verschleißfeste Kohlenstoffbeschichtungen (DLC bzw. ta-C) mit herausragenden Eigenschaften an.

Mit unserem Verfahren sind sehr hohe Schicht-Eindringhärten von bis zu 70 GPa (vgl. Diamant: H=100 GPa) realisierbar, wodurch die Beschichtungen äußerst widerstandsfähig gegen verschiedene Verschleißmechanismen sind.

Aufgrund der geringen Oberflächenrauheit und des dadurch niedrigen Reibungskoeffizienten sind diese Schichten auch für Anwendungen prädestiniert, bei denen eine möglichst geringe Reibung von entscheidender Bedeutung ist.

Die niedrigen Temperaturen während der Schichterzeugung (< 90 °C) ermöglichen es neben unterschiedlichen Metallen und Legierungen auch temperaturempfindliche Materialien wie z.B. Kunststoffe zu beschichten.

Neben dem Einsatz zum Verschleißschutz bieten unsere ta-C Schichten aufgrund ihrer chemischen Resistenz, Biokompatibilität, Strukturier- und Dotierbarkeit eine breite Palette an weiteren Anwendungsmöglichkeiten, bspw. in der Medizintechnik, Lebensmittelindustrie oder Sensorik.

Name: Collaborative Research Centre SFB 1277 University of Regensburg
Description:
Today’s electronics is mostly based on transport and optical properties of conventional semiconductors and metallic systems. However, in the past few years, novel classes of materials have been identified that might enable a paradigm shift for future electronics. Many of these materials have in common that their itinerant electrons exhibit (pseudo-)relativistic behaviour: in graphene, electrons behave as massless Dirac particles, enabling studies of relativistic phenomena “in a pencil trace”. In so-called topological insulators, the electron spin is locked to the electron momentum due to relativistic spin-orbit coupling. Moreover, relativistic spin-orbit coupling at interfaces, surfaces and in nanostructures gives rise to spin-orbit fields that strongly influence electrical transport and optics and enable novel topological phenomena.

In SFB 1277 we investigate the fundamental properties of these special electronic systems and the emergent relativistic effects they entail. Moreover, our common aim is to explore if and how the Dirac-like band structures and strong spin-orbit coupling in novel material classes and nanostructures can be exploited for future electronic concepts and lead to new, as yet unforeseen functionalities. Our common objective is to uncover electronic, transport, magnetic and optical properties of a variety of such materials and systems. These include molecules, carbon nanotubes and nanowires, two-dimensional crystals, topological insulators and superconductors. We put emphasis not only on steady-state phenomena but in particular also on novel (pseudo-)relativistic effects in the time and frequency domain.

Name: nanodiag BW
Description:
nanodiag BW is one of seven selected clusters funded by the BMBF (during the second selection process) with the aim of converting nanopore technology into innovative products and services of personalized medicine. By this, diseases such as cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular, mental, neurodegenerative can be detected much earlier and treated in a much more targeted manner.

The consortium of the cluster, coordinated by Hahn-Schickard, consists of well-known players such as the Freiburg University Hospital, the University of Freiburg, the Max Planck Institute for Immunobiology and Epigenetics, Freiburg and start-ups such as Ionera and Actome as well as other partners from Baden-Württemberg research organisations. They all focus on the research of nanopores as well as applying nanopore technology for future molecular diagnostics.

NanodiagBW enables groundbreaking innovation by interlacing application-oriented research such as epigenetics or microbiology with basic research in physics, biochemistry and physiology as well as the emerging possibilities of bioinformatics, molecular dynamic simulations, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning. Meanwhile, micro- and nanofluidics together with microelectronics help to build integrated systems for the user.

Name: Deutsche Vakuum-Gesellschaft e.V.
Description:
Vakuum, insbesondere aber die Vakuumtechnik, ist für verschiedenste Industrien und für weite Teile der Forschung und Entwicklung unverzichtbar. Aber auch  in vielen Bereichen des täglichen Lebens spielt Vakuumtechnik eine zentrale Rolle. So würde es ohne die Vakuumtechnik viele Selbstverständlichkeiten unseres modernen Lebens schlicht nicht geben. Die vakuumgestützten Wissenschaften und Technologien, deren Förderung wir uns zur Aufgabe gemacht haben, sind also keine Nische, sondern haben eine wahrhaft umfassende Bedeutung für unsere Gesellschaft. Das Bewusstsein dafür im Interesse der Weiterentwicklung der vakuumgestützten Wissenschaften und Technologien zu fördern, ist unsere Kernaufgabe. 
Als eingetragener, gemeinnütziger Verein können wir unabhängig von anderen Interessen agieren und arbeiten daran, der Vakuumtechnik auf gesellschaftlicher und politischer Ebene mehr Gehör zu verschaffen. 
Um dies zu erreichen, haben wir uns mit anderen nationalen Vakuumgesellschaften in der „International Union of Vacuum Science and Technology“ (IUVSTA) organisiert und können unsere Mitglieder auch auf internationaler Ebene vertreten. Zusätzlich zur IUVSTA pflegen wir enge und direkte Kontakte zur Deutschen Physikalischen Gesellschaft (DPG).

Name: Institute for Energy and Materials Processes - EMPI
Description:
Efficient, large-scale energy conversion and storage are topics of high societal relevance, as is the generation and processing of materials that make efficient energy conversion possible in the first place and that are as sustainable as possible. For future progress on these topics, the scientific fundamentals must be well understood and incorporated into the teaching of young scientists and scholars. Therefore, so research and teaching are closely linked at EMPI.

The Institute for Energy and Materials Processes, EMPI, lays the scientific foundations for energy conversion and storage, the production and processing of functional materials and materials, and the understanding of high-temperature processes. This begins with research into the details in small experimental plants and covers the entire process chain up to the industrial scale. Experimental investigations are accompanied by theory and simulations, as preparation as well as for the interpretation of experimental results.

In research, EMPI covers a wide range of scientific disciplines, including quantum chemistry, reaction kinetics, in situ diagnostics, thermodynamics, fluid dynamics modeling and simulation, and provides an experimental platform ranging from materials design to processing, utilization, and optimization, especially for applications in the energy context. A unique strength lies in the multiple cross-connections between the disciplines, the development of versatile scientific tools, and the expertise in the targeted transfer of fundamental findings into practically usable processes. EMPI aims to provide important research impulses internationally and nationally with its work, and also to be a regional cooperation partner for companies in the Rhine-Ruhr region in research and development.

Name: Biointerfaces Lab

Name: nano analytik GmbH
Description:
nano analytik is the technology driver in active-cantilever based atomic force microscopy (AFM). We are a manufacturer and supplier of high performance atomic force microscope instruments for R&D and diverse industrial applications.

We aim to simplify scanning probe techniques and ultimately make them faster, enabling groundbreaking research and unique solutions for industry. We are the market leader and your trusted partner in scanning probe technology systems based on active cantilevers. We have expanded and standardized the use of active cantilevers as a successful, state-of-the-art replacement for traditional OBD solutions - without compromising AFM performance. This eliminates limitations on sample size and mass, representing a major step toward simplifying AFM, increasing imaging and metrology throughput, and delivering extremely user-friendly AFMs with an excellent price-performance ratio.

Our activities combine development, manufacturing, and distribution to support the community with high-quality active cantilevers and scanning probe instruments that operate in liquids, air, or vacuum.

nanofabrication and have achieved scale as one of the leading experts in the production of atomic

Name: GATTAquant - DNA Nanotechnologies
Description:
The company focuses on probes for fast, easy and precise quantification of super-resolution systems.

These probes allow you to check the resolution of your microscope with a precision of a few nanometers. This level of precision is reached by using special nanostructures (so called DNA origami structures) as breadboards for placing single dye molecules in an exactly defined pattern.

Our innovative nanorulers allow a fast, easy and precise determination of resolution values in any common super-resolution system (STED, SIM, GSD, dSTORM, Blink microscopy, DNA-PAINT). On the one hand the instantaneous visible, significant result makes it easy for users to proof their microscope’s resolution and on the other hand provides an opportunity for microscope manufacturers to demonstrate the performance of their products in an eye-catching way.

To ensure an optimized gain as well as a maximal performance of the probe, we design our products individually according to your wishes, requests and intentions.

Therefore the continuous extension of our portfolio is the main focus of our company’s research.

If you need more information, you're welcome to visit www.gattaquant.com.

Name: Nanoforall
Description:
We have developed innovative and intelligent solutions that significantly reduce the cost of training and equipment, especially in Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM). This opens the door for everyone, including children, youth, and curious minds, to explore this fascinating world and experience nanoscience for themselves.
Our tools allow young learners to see and feel the nano-world, just like scientists do with professional AFM systems. They can scan surfaces, visualize nanoscale structures, and understand how AFM helps us study materials atom by atom, all through simple and accessible setups.
We promise children and young learners an interactive journey full of surprises, excitement, and discovery. By blending science with hands-on exploration, we help them unlock new horizons, ignite their scientific curiosity, and empower a new generation of innovators capable of leading the future.
NanoAmina’s Mission:
A nano-lab in every school... no, in every home! 
Just as microscopes, lenses, and tools of the micro-world have become essential parts of daily life and modern education, we at Nanoforall aim to make nanoscience and AFM just as accessible and widely available.
Our vision is to provide a simple, creative gateway into the world of nanotechnology, bringing AFM-based experiments and nanoscale exploration directly into classrooms and living rooms.
We strive for a future where:
 Every school has its own nano-lab
 Every home can offer nanoscience and AFM experiences
 Every child can explore the unseen world with ease
Because we believe that when young minds learn to observe the unobservable, they grow up ready to create the impossible.

Name: XanTec bioanalytics GmbH
Description:
XanTec bioanalytics GmbH develops the surface chemistry that makes label-free biosensing work.

We are a team of specialists in surface chemistry, organic synthesis, biology and physics, dedicated to one thing: engineering the bio-interface between your sample and the sensor.

Our portfolio covers four core product groups:

SPR sensor chips — including CMD, HC, NiHC His-tag capture, streptavidin, protein A/G, click chemistry and custom matrices — compatible with Biacore, Reichert, Bruker Sierra, Carterra LSA, Sartorius, BioNavis and other major SPR platforms.

SPR instruments — benchtop and research-grade SPR systems for kinetic characterisation, affinity measurement and fragment screening, supplied alongside matched chip chemistries for fully integrated workflows.

Microarray slides — functionalised glass slides for protein, antibody, peptide, DNA and glycan microarrays, with surface chemistries tuned for low background, high spot homogeneity and reproducible printing.

Nanometer biocoatings — functional surface modifications for plastic, glass and metal substrates, used in microfluidics, diagnostic assays and OEM device manufacturing.

From standard catalogue products to fully custom surface chemistries, we support biomolecular interaction analysis, kinetic characterisation, protein profiling and assay development worldwide — from method development through to OEM-scale production.

Based in Düsseldorf, Germany, used in labs across 40+ countries.

Name: In-Situ Microscopy Alliance
Description:
In-situ Microscopy Alliance (IMA) is a community of experts in electron microscopy and complementary analytical techniques with the goal of advancing technology and moving towards a sustainable future. 

The alliance is driven by analytical in-situ equipment producers and is supported by leading scientists working on sustainable materials, efficient energy storage solutions, and advanced semiconductors. 

IMA will host webinars and workshops about new techniques and specific applications, as well as provide opportunities for academic and industrial collaborations and networking.

Name: codixx AG
Description:
Driving Innovation Since 1998
codixx AG is a German company specializing in the development and production of high-quality polarizers for the ultraviolet, visible, and infrared spectral ranges.

Our products are based on a unique technology for embedding and processing nanoparticles in glass. In addition to our colorPol polarizers, our portfolio includes polymer polarizers, as well as wafers and substrates for analytical applications.

 Trusted by industries and researchers around the world.

Name: Surflay Nanotec GmbH
Description:
Surflay Nanotec GmbH is an interdisciplinary team of scientists transforming surface modification, characterization, LbL technologies, fluorescent polymers, nanoparticles, micro-particles, and micro-sensors into valuable products assessing pharmaceutical and non-pharmaceutical applications. Dr. Lars Dähne leads Surflay Nanotec since 2008, after the increased success of the development of the Layer-by-Layer encapsulation at the Max Planck Institute of Colloids and Interfaces. Surflay is at the cutting edge of polymer and surface science as well as micro-sensors, helping academic and industrial partners to develop highly valuable technologies and products. 

At Surflay Nanotec GmbH, our focus revolves around three interconnected scientific solutions. Firstly, we specialize in contract research and surface solutions, offering nanoscale surface modification and functionalization, as well as Layer-by-Layer (LbL) coatings. These advanced techniques allow for precise control over surface properties and can be tailored to meet specific requirements. Secondly, we excel in the development of fluorescent polymers, nano- and micro-structures, beads, and microbubbles. These innovative materials find applications in various fields, including imaging, diagnostics, and sensing. Lastly, we are experts in label-free microsensor systems, enabling the real-time monitoring of important parameters such as bioanalysis, pH, temperature, and oxygen levels, among others. 

If you are interested in any of our solutions or services, please do not hesitate to contact us. We offer tailored research and development services, and we are more than happy to provide further information about our products. Additionally, we provide analytical services and offer opportunities for licensing our cutting-edge technology. Furthermore, we are open to engaging in third-party-funded joint development projects to collaborate on innovative solutions in partnership with other organizations.

Name: CREAVAC PVD AG
Description:
Wir vereinen die Entwicklung und Fertigung von Beschichtungen im Hochvakuum mit dem Bau von Anlagen zur industriellen Beschichtung von Materialien wie Kunststoff, Glas, Wafer, Metallband oder flexiblen Substraten. Wir entwickeln unsere technologischen Grundlagen und Kompetenzen konsequent weiter, die entscheidend für unseren Unternehmenserfolg sind. Name: ISSPP e.V. | International Society for the Study of Pleura and Peritoneum
Description: ISSPP not only a scientific society, it is a project. One we hope will increase the awareness and the interest of the scientific and medical communities for pleura and peritoneum. We will grow, together and step-by-step, a high-quality and interdisciplinary knowledge base on pleura and peritoneum. We hope that talking together, exchanging results and criticism, standardizing measures and outcomes, and coordinating research efforts will lead to better therapies of the life-threatening diseases of pleura and peritoneum. Finally, it is allowed to dream that, in the long term, this new community of interest might obtain full recognition of pleura and peritoneum as organs of the human body.

Name: BalticNet-PlasmaTec
Description:
http://www.balticnet-plasmatec.org/legal-notice/

The BalticNet-PlasmaTec registered association stands for international technology and market-oriented cooperation of science, research and economics in the field of plasma technology and adjacent disciplines. One cluster aim is to increase the perception of the plasma technology in the society. It also helps interested parties in the Baltic Sea region assess their potential for using this technology. 
As an international cluster, BalticNet-PlasmaTec supports the creation of new jobs in the long term by introducing and disseminating the plasma technology in the universities, industry, SME and public facilities. This will be realised by development of new business segments, spin-offs and an intensive common marketing.
The BalticNet-PlasmTec based on 5 workgroups where different types of project will be realized. The work in the workgroup Plasma& Environment focused on plasma application for environment protection. The focus of the workgroup Plasma & Bio is the combination of physical plasmas with life science and medicine. Within the workgroup Vacuum Technology the members work with low pressure plasma applications. The Education workgroup organize education events for employees and students like summer schools, placements and workshops. All activities to increase the visibility of plasma and the growing of the cluster are bundled in the workgroup Marketing.

Name: Gesellschaft für Bioanalytik Münster e.V.
Description:
Bioanalytik-muenster is a regional network of
•universities 
•research centres 
•enterprises 
•transfer institutions 
•investors

which have joined forces in this non-profit-making organisation. 

Bioanalytik-muenster (founded in November 2000) provides a central communication and information platform for scientists, entrepreneurs, investors and members of the public who are interested in bioanalytics. 

Purpose

The purpose of the organisation is to promote science, research and education in the field of bioanalytics in the Münster region.

Aim

The aim of the organisation is to develop the Münster region into a leading bioanalytics location with the emphasis on nano-bioanalytics. From February 2004 to September 2008 bioanalytik-muenster coordinated together with the Atomic Energy Commisssion (CEA) in Grenoble the EC Network of Excellence Nano2Life to strengthen the European scientific and economic leadership in nanobiotechnology. By taking part in various EU projects the organisation expands its Network trans-regionally.
